results.text: ENERGY COMMODITY MARKETS OUTLOOK | OCTOBER 2026 14 Oil Recent developments In mid-October, front-month Brent futures reached about $110 per barrel (bbl) as markets weighed rising crude supply and an accelerated release of emergency oil stockpiles by International Energy Agency (IEA) members against conflict in the Middle East (figure 7.A). Entering October, average Middle East oil exports approached their 2025 level owing to greater use of ship-to-ship transfers and untracked shipments (figure 7.B). events.query: growth in global natural gas production forecast for 2027

results.text: ENERGYCOMMODITY MARKETS OUTLOOK | OCTOBER 2026 21 Global natural gas production is projected to decline by 0.8 percent (35 bcm) in 2026. A drop of more than 11 percent (90 bcm) in the Middle East—driven by damage to gas-processing and LNG facilities—is expected to be partly offset by increases of 3.2 percent (42 bcm) in North America and 2.1 percent (18 bcm) in Eurasia. Global production is forecast to increase by about 2.5 percent (110 bcm) in 2027, led by nearly a 5.5 percent (39 bcm) recovery in the Middle East, with the region’s output expected to remain below its 2025 level because of reduced LNG export capacity in Qatar and delays to its North Field expansion. Production is also expected to rise by 3 percent (41 bcm) in North America, 2 percent (15 bcm) in Asia Pacific, and 1 percent (10 bcm) in Eurasia.

In contrast, the U.S. benchmark is projected to remain unchanged in 2026 (y/y), and to increase by about 6 percent in 2027 and about 5 percent in 2028, mainly driven by growing external demand for LNG. Global natural gas consumption is projected to decline by about 1 percent (50 bcm) in 2026 (figure 10.D). Demand is expected to decrease by about 8 percent (50 bcm) in the Middle East, reflecting disrupted industrial demand. In Europe and Asia Pacific, consumption is set to soften by 2.5 percent (13 bcm) and about 1 percent (9 bcm), respectively, as power-sector use declines. By contrast, Eurasian demand is projected to rise as residential consumption rebounds after mild weather in 2025.

On this basis, absent additional lasting damage to oil infrastructure, global oil production is projected at about 106 mb/d in 2027, returning the market to a substantial surplus in the second quarter. European natural gas prices, after surging by a projected 58 percent (y/y) this year to $19 per million British thermal units ($/mmbtu), are expected to fall by only 8 percent next year to $17.5/mmbtu—a large upward revision from the April forecast. Higher-for-longer prices, relative to oil, reflect production prospects for LNG, which FIGURE 4 Outlook for commodity markets Global commodity prices are set to increase by an average of 23 percent in 2026 before retreating by 7 percent in 2027 . The recovery of global oil consumption in 2027 is projected to be tepid, partly because an accelerated shift to electric vehicles is likely to have a lasting effect.

Even so, total grain supplies (production and beginning stocks combined) in 2026-27 are projected to be the second largest on record and about 3 percent higher than two years earlier, which should limit price increases compared with past episodes of grain market stress. Among grains, price pressures are most pronounced for wheat, amid several headwinds to production and trade. Wheat prices are projected to jump by 28 percent in 2026 and 14 percent in 2027, before easing by 11 percent in 2028. Global wheat output is expected to contract by 3 percent in 2026–27 with reduced harvests in several major producing countries.

answer: The projected year-on-year copper price increase for 2026 is 33 percent. Following this increase, copper prices are forecast to decline by 2 percent in 2027 and 4 percent in 2028, while remaining near record highs [world-bank-cmo-2026-10:50:paragraph-900:1].

events.query: copper price increase projected for 2026 before declines in 2027 and 2028

results.text: Copper mine production growth is expected to remain subdued, reflecting the lingering effects of weather-related disruptions in Indonesia, together with operational constraints and declining ore grades in Chile, the world’s largest producer. Export restrictions in the Democratic Republic of Congo could also constrain copper concentrate trade. Global copper demand declined slightly in the first half of 2026 but is expected to firm in 2027–28, supported by investment in power grids and data centers, as well as the continuing auto- industry pivot toward EV production, which is more copper-intensive. After a projected 33 percent (y/y) increase to a record annual average in 2026, copper prices are forecast to decline by 2 percent in 2027 and 4 percent in 2028 but remain near record highs.

METALS AND MINERALS COMMODITY MARKETS OUTLOOK | OCTOBER 2026 42 2027 and 3 percent in 2028 as Gulf production gradually recovers and additional capacity in Africa and Asia comes online. Copper prices rose by 6 percent in 2026Q3 (q/q) and strengthened further in October to new record highs. The rally partly reflects mining disruptions and dislocations between major refined copper markets. Earlier in 2026, uncertainty over possible U.S. tariffs on refined copper imports generated a sizable premium of COMEX copper prices over LME prices. The resulting arbitrage drew refined copper into U.S. warehouses, tightening availability elsewhere and putting upward pressure on LME prices (figure 19.C). Although the COMEX-LME differential narrowed substantially by September, uncertainty persists over whether tariffs will take effect in January 2027, with COMEX inventories around all-time highs.

The metals and minerals index is projected to edge 3 percent (y/y) lower in 2027 as supply conditions improve somewhat for several base metals owing to fading production or export disruptions and new capacity coming on stream. For copper, however, mined supply growth is anticipated to remain subdued, reflecting factors such as declining ore grades in Chile, the world’s largest producer. Assuming global economic growth holds up, buoyant base metal demand driven by, for example, the expansion of renewable energy infrastructure, electric vehicles, and data centers is likely to keep medium-term prices elevated (figure 4.F). Precious metal prices are also expected to register a steep average increase of 40 percent in 2026, amid strong demand for diversifying financial assets against a strained geopolitical backdrop. answer: In the Special Focus, the commodity groups identified as net transmitters of price volatility include industrial metals (notably copper), food commodities (such as maize), and precious metals (like silver). Conversely, livestock and soft commodities are categorized as net receivers of price volatility, receiving considerably more volatility than they transmit. Energy and precious metals occupy an intermediate position, transmitting and receiving similar amounts of volatility, although their roles can vary in specific episodes, such as during COVID-19 when they became net transmitters while food became a net receiver [world-bank-cmo-2026-10:57:paragraph-900:3][world-bank-cmo-2026-10:62:paragraph-900:3].

results.text: FERTILIZERSCOMMODITY MARKETS OUTLOOK | OCTOBER 2026 39 Recent developments Nitrogen (urea) prices averaged $399/mt in 2026Q3, down 42 percent (q/q) and 18 percent (y/y), after peaking at $857/mt in April (figure 18.A). Prices eased further in the first half of October. The initial retreat during 2026Q2 reflected China’s easing of export restrictions in May, the temporary reduction in hostilities following the June memorandum of understand- ing between the United States and the Islamic Republic of Iran, and reductions in purchases, partly owing to the end of spring planting in the Northern Hemisphere. Increased exports from China and other major suppliers, including Egypt, Nigeria, and Oman, helped sustain a return to more normal price levels. China’s urea exports are expected to reach 7.0 million metric tons (mmt) in 2026, up from 4.9 mmt in 2025.

Urea prices are forecast to fall by 16 percent in 2027 and 14 percent in 2028, assuming Middle Eastern exports recover, natural gas prices ease, Fertilizers The World Bank Group’s fertilizer price index fell by 22 percent in 2026Q3 (q/q) and continued to decline in October, fully reversing the 2026Q2 surge that followed the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Urea prices drove both swings, while other fertilizer prices rose less sharply but remained elevated in 2026Q3. Despite the recent retreat, the index is projected to rise by about 14 percent in 2026 (y/y), reflecting shipping disruptions in the Middle East, associated increases in input costs, and trade restrictions. Prices are forecast to fall by 12 percent in 2027 and a further 8 percent in 2028 as input costs ease and supplies recover, aided by increased exports from producers outside the Gulf region.

Upside risks to the outlook for urea prices include an escalation in the Middle East conflict that raises input costs, particularly for natural gas, above baseline expectations. More specifically, continued conflict could lead to an extension of Qatar’s force majeure, imposed in March, on contracts to sell LNG and related products, including urea. Export restrictions by major producers are another potential source of renewed price surges. Conversely, a swift reduction of geopolitical tensions in the Gulf region could lead to a surge of exports, materially lowering prices, although infrastructure damage is likely to delay the full recovery of urea production. After a projected 7 percent increase in 2026, DAP prices are forecast to drop by about 18 percent in 2027 and 17 percent in 2028.

Other critical minerals Prices of other critical minerals generally weakened in 2026Q3, led by cobalt, which fell by 25 percent (q/q), and lithium, which declined by 13 percent (figure 20.A). The decline in lithium prices reflected the restart of previously curtailed mines in Australia, the resumption of concentrate exports from Zimbabwe, and softer EV sales momentum in China, although strong demand from energy storage and robust EV demand in several other regions provided support. Cobalt prices fell sharply, partly reversing earlier gains, but remained elevated as export quotas in the Democratic Republic of Congo continued to constrain global supply. Rare earth prices were broadly stable, with ongoing Chinese export controls and licensing requirements curbing supply in some markets outside China.

Nickel demand from battery production, however, is being tempered by the growing use of nickel-free lithium-iron-phosphate batteries in EVs and energy storage. After a projected 13 percent increase in 2026 (y/y), nickel prices are forecast to be little changed in 2027 as market conditions rebalance, before firming by 1 percent in 2028. Tin prices rose by 4 percent in 2026Q3 (q/q), reaching all-time highs amid persistent supply constraints, and remained broadly stable in October. Tin supply is expected to recover gradually as mine production continues to normalize in Myanmar following policy-related disruptions, and regulatory and export constraints ease in Indonesia. Rising tin output should ease the market tightness seen in 2026, although limited expansion among other producers and a thin pipeline of new mining projects are expected to constrain future supply growth.

The decline in lithium prices reflected the restart of previously curtailed mines in Australia, the resumption of concentrate exports from Zimbabwe, and softer EV sales momentum in China, although strong demand from energy storage and robust EV demand in several other regions provided support. Cobalt prices fell sharply, partly reversing earlier gains, but remained elevated as export quotas in the Democratic Republic of Congo continued to constrain global supply. Rare earth prices were broadly stable, with ongoing Chinese export controls and licensing requirements curbing supply in some markets outside China.

Nickel demand from battery production, however, is being tempered by the growing use of nickel-free lithium-iron-phosphate batteries in EVs and energy storage. After a projected 13 percent increase in 2026 (y/y), nickel prices are forecast to be little changed in 2027 as market conditions rebalance, before firming by 1 percent in 2028. Tin prices rose by 4 percent in 2026Q3 (q/q), reaching all-time highs amid persistent supply constraints, and remained broadly stable in October. Tin supply is expected to recover gradually as mine production continues to normalize in Myanmar following policy-related disruptions, and regulatory and export constraints ease in Indonesia. Rising tin output should ease the market tightness seen in 2026, although limited expansion among other producers and a thin pipeline of new mining projects are expected to constrain future supply growth.
